walkthroughs.body_html:
Ethical Legal Cultural Issues — a core area of GCSE Computer Science.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Ethical Legal Cultural Issues brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Ethical Legal Cultural Issues.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Open source software is software whose:
options: Source code is available for anyone to view, modify and redistribute
Source code is a closely guarded secret
Licence forbids any copying
Code is written only in binary
Buy a licence that restricts copying and modification
Receive the full source code to edit
Own the software outright
May resell unlimited copies

mcqs.q: Which is the best example of a CULTURAL impact of technology?
options: Social media changing how people communicate and socialise
A virus deleting files on a server
A faster graphics card being released
A longer USB cable standard

mcqs.q: Under the Data Protection Act 2018, organisations must:
options: Keep personal data accurate and secure, and use it lawfully and fairly
Publish all customer data online
Delete all data every week
Share data freely with any company that asks

mcqs.q: Does open source always mean free of charge?
options: Yes - ownership transfers as soon as you install it.
No - open source refers to access to the source code; companies can and do charge for open-source products, support and services.
Yes - open source and free of charge are the same thing.
Yes - it is illegal to sell open-source software.

mcqs.q: Is hacking into a system an offence under the Data Protection Act?
options: No - unauthorised access is an offence under the Computer Misuse Act 1990; the Data Protection Act governs how organisations handle personal data.
Yes - the Data Protection Act is the law that bans hacking.
Yes - hacking is only covered by copyright law.
Yes - it is illegal to sell open-source software.

mcqs.q: When you buy proprietary software, do you own it?
options: Yes - it is illegal to sell open-source software.
No - you buy a licence to use it under set conditions; the publisher keeps ownership of the software and its source code.
Yes - buying software makes it your property to copy and resell.
Yes - ownership transfers as soon as you install it.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Open source software”?
options: UK law criminalising unauthorised access to computer systems and data, and the creation or use of malware to impair computers.
A question of right and wrong raised by technology, such as invasive data collection, algorithmic bias or monitoring employees.
Software whose source code is made available so anyone can study, modify and redistribute it under the terms of its licence.
A way technology changes how groups of people live and interact, such as social media altering communication, news and relationships.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Proprietary software”?
options: Software whose source code is made available so anyone can study, modify and redistribute it under the terms of its licence.
A way technology changes how groups of people live and interact, such as social media altering communication, news and relationships.
A question of right and wrong raised by technology, such as invasive data collection, algorithmic bias or monitoring employees.
Software whose source code is kept private; users buy a licence that restricts how the software may be used, copied or modified.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Computer Misuse Act 1990”?
options: UK law requiring organisations to process personal data fairly, lawfully, accurately and securely, and giving individuals rights over their data.
UK law criminalising unauthorised access to computer systems and data, and the creation or use of malware to impair computers.
A question of right and wrong raised by technology, such as invasive data collection, algorithmic bias or monitoring employees.
Software whose source code is made available so anyone can study, modify and redistribute it under the terms of its licence.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Data Protection Act 2018”?
options: UK law criminalising unauthorised access to computer systems and data, and the creation or use of malware to impair computers.
UK law requiring organisations to process personal data fairly, lawfully, accurately and securely, and giving individuals rights over their data.
A question of right and wrong raised by technology, such as invasive data collection, algorithmic bias or monitoring employees.
Software whose source code is kept private; users buy a licence that restricts how the software may be used, copied or modified.

options: Software whose source code is made available so anyone can study, modify and redistribute it under the terms of its licence.
UK law criminalising unauthorised access to computer systems and data, and the creation or use of malware to impair computers.

options: A question of right and wrong raised by technology, such as invasive data collection, algorithmic bias or monitoring employees.
